sources.entry: JUMP - Keyboard-driven navigation that labels every clickable element so you can click, scroll and search any app without the mouse.

summary.one_liner: JUMP is a macOS menu bar app for keyboard-driven navigation that labels clickable elements on screen so you can click, scroll, and search without a mouse.
summary.what_it_does: JUMP runs in the macOS menu bar. Pressing ⌘⇧Space in the focused window labels every clickable element with a short key sequence, and typing a label clicks that element. Narrowing keys filter the visible labels as you type. A scroll mode (⌘⇧J) scrolls the focused window with vim-style keys, and a text search mode (⌘⇧F) finds visible text and moves between matches. Modifiers held while choosing a label change the click action, for example Shift for right-click and ⌘ for double-click. An optional OCR fallback recognizes text in windows without usable Accessibility text, and it needs Screen Recording permission only when enabled. The app offers several hint themes, label sizes, and Liquid Glass styles.
use_cases: click any on-screen button or link with the keyboard
scroll a macOS window without a mouse
search visible text in an app by keyboard
click items in terminals or PDFs using OCR
replace mouse use for repetitive UI navigation
how_to_run: Download JUMP.dmg from the releases page, open it, and drag JUMP to Applications
Open JUMP and allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility
For development: brew install xcodegen, then run xcodegen generate and open JUMP.xcodeproj
notable: Three modes: hint clicking, vim-style scrolling, and text search, each with its own shortcut
Modifier keys choose the click action (right-click, double-click, move pointer only) and clicks wait until the modifier is released
Optional OCR fallback for terminals, PDFs and images; captures stay in memory
Credits Vimac by Dexter Leng as its predecessor and builds on its ideas and code
Core logic is in a separate Swift package that is tested without launching the app
caveats: Requires macOS 26 or later and Xcode 27 or later to build
Not yet notarized by Apple, so macOS blocks the first launch and the user must approve it manually
Needs Accessibility permission; development builds need a personal Apple Development certificate or the permission is lost on each rebuild
Status is v1.1.0 and the README points to a design spec and roadmap in my-idea.md
